name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+15 district with no Republican nominee on the ballot
Menendez has raised $2.2 million with outside support; challengers report no fundraising
Polymarket prices a Democratic win near 95 percent
Residual voter unease tied to the Menendez family name is the main drag
model.rationale: A fifteen-point Democratic lean combined with the absence of a major-party opponent leaves Aristotle Eliopoulos and the other independents with no plausible path, and prediction markets price the incumbent near 95 percent. Only the family-name baggage and an untested ballot keep this from being a total lock.
model.watch: A late influx of coordinated funding behind Eliopoulos, or fresh headlines tying Rob Menendez to his father's legal troubles, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
NJ-08, anchored in Hudson County, leans Democratic by fifteen points. Rob Menendez, first elected in 2022, seeks a third term with about $2.2 million raised and outside groups adding more than $900,000 in support. No Republican filed; his principal challenger is an independent, joined by two other minor-candidate opponents with no reported fundraising.

The ballot itself does most of the work here, since a district this Democratic rarely elects a non-Democrat even in strong Republican years. Prediction markets put Menendez's winning chances near 95 percent. The main variables are turnout drop-off and lingering association with his father's corruption case, but neither plausibly closes a double-digit structural gap. The seat is rated Safe Democratic.
